verdict: The targeted technical fixes are credible and preserve the character's anatomy. No blocker was found in the inspected code, still evidence or current standalone exports. The original sad/worried mouth reset and mathematical mid-descent stop are resolved. Broader transition-family intent and final perceived landing quality still need bounded playback review; those unknowns do not invalidate the static assets.
inspectedEvidence: Compared animation-v5/character.js, motion.js and motion.test.mjs against reviews/2026-11-07-refinement/before; read source/applications-v5.js:1–64.
Fresh evidence: poses.png, sad-worried.png, worried-sad.png, excited.png, all-24.png and identity.png. These are rendered pose sheets, not continuous playback.
Fresh execution of motion.test.mjs: all nine tests passed.
Parsed all four exported V5 SVGs: zero duplicate IDs individually or when combining the four distinct variants. Repeating the same header variant would repeat its eleven IDs.
resolvedIssues: Night anatomy is preserved: the renderer diff adds two behind-antenna edge paths, both copying the existing deformed d exactly. Existing head, torso, mitten, foot and wing paths, pivots and proportions are unchanged. The new 16-unit stroke expands painted edge coverage, not the underlying anatomical path (character.js:137–148,254–258). Identity evidence now shows connected stems at the inspected night sizes.

Thinking, focused and worried gain useful mitten separation through coordinates alone. Thinking retains its acting mitten at the cheek while lowering the supporting one; focused has two low separated mittens. The before/after sheet supports clearer staging without larger hands or longer arms. Grateful intentionally retains a paired gesture.

Sad→worried and its reverse no longer show the old open green-mouth interval in the inspected updated rows. Tests sample both transitions every 5 ms through 1100 ms and verify closed/non-positive mouth, lowered head and concerned brows (motion.test.mjs:128–147).

Excited bodyY now passes through 900 ms with matched nonzero descent velocity. Its 720/900/1060 ms positions and hop height remain unchanged; wings retain their independent reversal. The new tests establish monotonic bounded descent and velocity continuity at that intermediate key (motion.test.mjs:174–191).

findings.claim: The family rule is broader than the two demonstrated transition fixes: it inherits nearly all posture and facial channels across six difficult and four reflective feelings, including same-feeling replay. Numeric compatibility is not evidence that every inherited hand pose, accessory or anticipation serves the new intention.
findings.fix: Keep the implementation provisionally. Review angry↔scared, thinking→confused and thinking replay before using those combinations; narrow channels or add pair exceptions only where a visible intention problem appears.
findings.verification: Requested root captures at 0/200/400/800 ms plus normal-speed playback should show purposeful anticipation and accessory behavior, without unwanted pose retention.

findings.claim: Export ID repair correctly separates the current four variants, but the comment promising protection when two exports are inlined is overbroad. The namespace contains kind/theme, not instance identity; two identical variants repeat IDs.
findings.fix: Document standalone/img use, or namespace each insertion if repeated inline instances are supported. Current PNG README and separate SVG files are unaffected.
findings.verification: If inline repetition becomes a supported use, combine two identical variants and assert unique IDs plus correctly resolved paint, clipping and accessibility references.

limits: No peer refinement reviews were read. No production files changed and no browser was operated by this reviewer.

Continuous updated reel/transition proof was pending. Landing intentionally changes velocity to zero at ground contact; sampled poses and tests cannot establish its perceived softness. Keyboard behavior belongs to the interaction review, not this rig approval.
